body:
# Incident: Mislabelled Allergen Container in the Walk-in (Prep)

Owner: Samuel Okafor (Sous Chef, Prep)

## 1) Purpose and Scope
- Document the mislabelled allergen incident and lock in fixes.
- Applies to Prep station, with touchpoints at Pass, Grill, Pastry, and Front of House.
- Goal: zero allergen mislabels; every item correctly labelled, stored, and verified.

## 2) Incident Summary
- Item involved: Pesto (contains pine nuts; tree nut allergen).
- Incorrect label: “Basil Oil.”
- Where found: At the pass during pre-service checks.
- Action taken: Service stop for that item, container pulled, product discarded, area sanitized, stock re-checked.
- Exposure: None. Product did not reach a guest or a plate.

## 3) Timeline of Events
| Time Marker | Event |
|---|---|
| T-Prep | Prep cook blends pesto (basil, pine nuts, parmesan, oil), transfers to a 1-qt deli. |
| T-Prep+ | Container is labelled “Basil Oil” and placed on Prep walk-in shelf with oils. |
| T-Pass Check | Sous Chef at the pass reviews mise and spots pesto texture inconsistent with basil oil; calls “Allergen Stop.” |
| T+5 min | Container quarantined to Dish area; new basil oil requested; inventory audit on herb oils and nut-based sauces. |
| T+12 min | Pesto confirmed by taste/recipe check; product discarded; contact surfaces sanitized. |
| T+20 min | All labels on related items corrected; team briefed; service proceeds. |

## 4) People Involved by Role
- Prep: Prep Cook (assembled and labelled), Samuel Okafor (Sous Chef, identified mislabel, led response).
- Grill: Grill Lead (paused pull from herb oil par level; confirmed no cross-use).
- Pastry: Pastry Cook (verified nut storage integrity; no impact).
- Front of House: Floor Manager (updated allergen briefing to servers; confirmed no guest exposure).

## 5) Root Cause Analysis
- Primary cause: Wrong product selected on the pre-printed label stack; pesto container received a “Basil Oil” label.
- Contributing factors:
  - Pesto and basil oil produced during same block; containers side by side.
  - Similar appearance (green, oily surface) reduced visual discrimination.
  - Single-person label application; no second check.
  - Allergen color code not applied (pesto should carry an allergen color label and an “TREE NUT” callout).
- Not observed:
  - No time/temperature abuse.
  - No guest exposure.

## 6) Product Handling and Disposition
1) Quarantine: Remove suspect container from food areas. Place in a bus tub labeled “Hold – Allergen Review.”
2) Confirm contents: Match against recipe (pine nuts visible; taste if needed by Sous only, using clean spoon). Do not reintroduce.
3) Discard: Dispose of entire container into compost/trash per station rules. Do not strain or repurpose.
4) Sanitize: Clean and sanitize any shelf, cambro lid, and pass surface that contacted the container.
   - Use quat at 200–400 ppm or chlorine at 50–100 ppm; 1-minute contact time; air dry.
5) Replace: Make fresh basil oil in a clean container with correct label; store on non-allergen shelf.
6) Audit: Check all herb oils, pestos, nut sauces, and green sauces in the walk-in and lowboy for correct labels and color tags.

## 7) Immediate Corrective Actions (What we do now)
1) Stop and call: “Allergen Stop – Mislabel” at the pass. Communicate to all stations.
2) Pull the item and any sister containers (same prep block) from service.
3) Re-label any affected items with correct names, allergen callouts, and color tags.
4) Log incident in Prep incident log with product, station, shift code, and initials.
5) Huddle: 2-minute team brief on what changed and where the safe replacement is stored.

## 8) Preventive Measures and Controls
- Two-person label check (mandatory on allergen items and all green sauces):
  1) Cook fills container and writes/places label.
  2) Second set of eyes (lead or another cook) verifies product name, allergen callout, color tag, and initials the label.
- Label content standard (all containers):
  - Product name (exact): “Pesto – TREE NUT (Pine Nut)”, “Basil Oil (No Allergen)”.
  - Shift code, maker initials.
  - Prep area: “Prep”.
- Storage segregation:
  - Allergen items on dedicated lower shelf, right side of Prep walk-in; non-allergen herb oils on upper middle shelf.
  - Keep lids on; no stacking allergens above non-allergens.
- Make/batch separation:
  - Do not produce pesto and basil oil simultaneously in the same zone. Finish one, label, stow, wipe, then start the next.
- Visual cues (color and icons):

| Label Color | Use Case | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Red | Allergen present (nuts, dairy, eggs, gluten, shellfish, soy, sesame) | “Pesto – TREE NUT (Pine Nut)” |
| Yellow | Allergen control in progress/hold | “Hold – Review” |
| Green | Herb oils/sauces with no major allergens | “Basil Oil (No Allergen)” |

- Tool discipline:
  - Dedicated red-lidded delis for nut-based sauces.
  - Red-handled spatulas for allergens; store in allergen bin.
- Pass check reinforcement:
  - Sous verifies texture/aroma vs label on all green sauces before service.

## 9) Verification, Training, and Audit
- Daily: Prep Lead spot-checks 5 random containers (at least 2 green sauces) for correct name, color, allergen callout, and initials.
- Weekly: Samuel reviews allergen shelf for drift (items, positions, labels) and documents findings.
- Training: Line talk covers color code and two-person check; new hires walk through the label flow with a trainer before solo work.
- Success metric: 0 mislabels in walk-in audits; any fail triggers immediate retrain.

## 10) Communication to Front of House
- FOH gets an immediate update if an allergen item is pulled or replaced.
- Servers instructed to confirm nut presence verbally on any dish listing pesto until replacement verified.

## 11) Closing Note
This was caught before service. Keep the two-person check and color code tight. When in doubt, stop, verify, and relabel before anything leaves Prep.
summary: Mislabelled pesto as basil oil caught at the pass; product discarded; root causes fixed with color labels, two-person checks, and storage segregation.
title: Incident: Mislabelled Allergen Container in the Walk-in
